newsitem.title: USA: Clinton asks for hearing on Labor Secretary nominee.
newsitem.headline: Clinton asks for hearing on Labor Secretary nominee.

text.p: President Clinton said Thursday the Senate Labour Committee should schedule hearings for Alexis Herman, his nominee for Labour Secretary.

Clinton went out of his way to defend his choice. Unprompted, he told reporters that Herman, a former White House director of the Office of Public Liaison, deserved a prompt hearing. He has also urged the Senate to hold hearings soon on Anthony Lake, his nominee for director of the Central Intelligence Agency.

"There has still not been a hearing," Clinton said. "I think that's a big mistake. She has wide support among labour -- labour unions endorsed her yesterday -- and she has wide support among business."
"She is clearly well qualified ... and if she gets a hearing, she will be confirmed," Clinton said.
Herman is the only black woman nominated to a cabinet post in Clinton's second-term.

Senate Republicans have raised questions about whether she violated the law when her office invited a federal banking regulator to a political "coffee" meeting at the White House with Clinton and some bankers.
Vermont Republican James Jeffords, chairman of the Senate Labour Committee, has not said when hearings will be held.
The AFL-CIO Wednesday issued a statement calling for a hearing on her nomination, saying she was being "held hostage".
